title: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new watermarks will work
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: How will the watermarking actually work? Can it be hidden with editing? And how does this affect code?
body:
Anthropic has provided additional information on the implementation of watermarks in the text generated by its chatbot, Claude. The watermarking process involves creating a pattern in the responses that is undetectable to readers but can be identified by those with a decoding key. This is achieved through "low-stakes choices" in word selection, such as choosing between synonyms. The company has clarified that watermarking does not affect the quality of Claude's output, and a watermarked response is indistinguishable from an unwatermarked one.

The watermarking approach used by Anthropic is based on the SynthID-Text method outlined by the Google DeepMind team in 2024. The company plans to release a watermark detection API, which will enable the identification of watermarked text. It is worth noting that watermarking is distinct from AI detection approaches that rely on identifying patterns in writing, such as those offered by companies like Pangram. 
* The SynthID-Text approach is used for watermarking
* A watermark detection API will be released
* Watermarking is distinct from AI detection approaches

## Why this matters
The introduction of watermarks in Claude's generated text has significant implications for the transparency and accountability of AI-generated content. By providing a means to identify AI-generated text, Anthropic is taking a step towards compliance with the EU AI Act's Transparency Code. However, the effectiveness of this approach in preventing the misuse of AI-generated content remains to be seen, as users may still attempt to hide or remove the watermarks through editing or rewriting.
